title: Harmful Agent Handoffs and Safe Coordination
subtitle: A Controlled Study of Transfer and Verification
author: Frank Peterlein
abstract: Can harmful plans survive replacement through handoff notes, and can successors reject them while coordinating? We study a transparent four-agent allocation task. Originals are instructed to favor their coalition at outsiders’ expense; neutral successors receive controlled note combinations. In a format-expanded analysis, a prespecified paired-note contrast increases joint harm by 0.50 for Qwen and 0.43 for GPT-OSS relative to facts alone, across five and seven complete cases. Verification reduces joint harm but increases duplicate claims relative to coordinated harmful notes. A post-hoc comparison finds the same duplicate frequency under verification and facts alone. Structural and fixed-note controls improve safe coordination through task changes or shared decision rules. A final fresh factorial control crosses harmful-note and reminder presence while holding the rule fixed. Among 79 valid episodes, three partial outsider harms occur only with harmful notes and no reminder; all other valid episodes are safe-optimal. The primary safe-optimal interaction is +0.125 across four complete Qwen cases and +0.200 across five GPT-OSS cases. These selected cohorts support inherited instructed-plan transfer and conditional benefits from verification plus a shared safe convention, without establishing spontaneous collusion or a general defense.

blocks.text: 1. Introduction

Agent replacement does not remove the information left by the outgoing agents. Handoff notes can preserve useful conventions, but they can also carry recommendations that benefit a coalition at other participants’ expense. The Inherited Collusion project asks whether such instructed harmful plans affect neutral successors, and whether verification can prevent harm without disrupting task coordination.

The distinction matters because rejecting a harmful recommendation does not itself select a common safe alternative. We first vary which original notes reach two independent successors. Three follow-up controls then investigate task structure, shared safe rules and the separate effects of notes and verification. The contribution is a bounded empirical audit of this handoff channel: enacted harm, task completion and coordination quality are measured separately.
2. Related Work

Colosseum distinguishes expressed collusive plans from enacted coalition-favoring behavior [1,4]. Self-Propagating Misalignment studies harmful goals passed to neutral successors and discusses utility costs of memory defenses [2]. Salami Attack studies jointly effective memory fragments [3]. Building on this work, we control delivery of role-specific notes written after enacted harmful or legitimate allocations, then measure coalition benefit, outsider harm and task coordination separately.

Shared conventions and symmetry breaking are established coordination approaches. Theory of Scene addresses collisions among homogeneous concurrent agents using public roles and shared task context [5]. Tacit Coordination of Large Language Models studies focal points and coordination without communication [6]. Our focused question is how these ideas behave in the presence of harmful inherited notes. The three follow-up controls distinguish task structure, an explicit public safe decision policy and the note-by-reminder interaction under that policy; earlier legitimate-source comparisons assess useful cooperation.
3. Methods

Two model agents, A and B, independently choose one of four tasks without seeing each other’s choice. Scripted outsiders C and D then minimize their combined cost on two distinct unclaimed tasks. Every agent earns 100 minus its task cost; an extra duplicate claim incurs a 200-point penalty shared by claimants. Neutral successors are instructed to maximize distinct task completion and then minimize total cost across all four agents. They receive the full public cost matrix and all 16 possible A/B outcomes, including the scripted continuation.

Here operational collusion means an enacted joint allocation that benefits A/B while reducing C/D reward relative to the cooperative reference. A joint-harm event requires both outsider specialties to be taken with positive coalition gain and outsider loss. Original agents are explicitly instructed to execute harmful or legitimate joint plans before writing role-specific notes to their replacements. This induces the original coalition; it does not establish spontaneous collusion. Successors receive neutral instructions and unchanged public facts. We also score continuous outsider loss, team reward, duplicate claims and safe-optimal completion. A safe optimum completes four distinct tasks at globally minimum total cost; zero joint harm alone can conceal partial outsider harm.

The handoff audit plans eight cost cases per model and two successor draws per route. Routes deliver facts alone, one note, both notes from the same original branch, crossed branches, or both notes plus a reminder to check them against public rules and total cost. Two role-swapped original-plan orientations (p0 and p1) and legitimate-source controls test convention transfer. Each model supplies its own originals and successors, so differences between models combine sender and recipient behavior. All main studies use Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and GPT-OSS-120B at temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95 and an 8,192-token output limit; exact identifiers and provenance limits are in Appendix B.

The original strict audit retains 360/512 planned episodes. A disclosed post-start format amendment accepts one complete outer JSON fence and recovers 439/512 episodes by reusing exact old responses and calling only previously undispatched slots. Four unresolved requests remain missing. We report both populations separately; the amended analysis is not an independent replication. Later controls were locally frozen before their own responses, after the earlier findings were known. Internal version names, dates, eligibility rules and all missingness are mapped in Appendices B and H.

The structural control plans six new cases per model, two draws per condition, both original objectives and three routes: facts alone, both original notes and verified notes. Adding one unit to two nonpreferred safe A/B cost cells creates a unique safe optimum while preserving optimal total cost and assigned original-plan outcomes. Public outcome tables are recomputed and originals write fresh notes for each structure. Four Qwen cases and all six GPT-OSS cases complete this control; one technically valid but semantically incorrect Qwen diagnostic remains included. The intervention therefore changes both cost geometry and the notes produced.

The fixed-note control instead holds the symmetric matrices and exact notes from those ten available donor cases fixed. Fresh successors receive verification alone or verification plus a shared rule: choose the lexicographically first or last A/B task pair among public outcomes with maximum distinct completion and minimum total cost. Both original objectives and two draws per arm are retained. Its primary harmful-mode contrast averages the two directions equally, subtracts fresh verification alone and weights complete cases equally within each model. The directions are fixed subconditions, not independent replications. Logical completion ranges cover missing outcomes in the available cohort; they are not confidence intervals or corrections for donor selection.

The final factorial control reuses the same ten symmetric donor cases with entirely fresh successors. Harmful notes are either supplied or omitted, crossed with the unchanged verification reminder being present or absent. Every arm contains the shared safe rule, tested once in each fixed direction. The primary safe-optimal contrast is the reminder effect with notes minus its effect without notes, averaging directions within each case and weighting the same complete cases equally within each model. There are no new originals, diagnostic probes or legitimate-note arms.
4. Results

Inherited harmful-plan transfer. In the format-expanded audit, both same-source notes from orientation p0 increase joint-harm probability relative to facts alone by 0.50 for Qwen across five complete cases and 0.43 for GPT-OSS across seven. The strict counterparts are 0.50 over only one case and 0.43 over seven. These are within-case delivery contrasts, not population estimates. One-note and crossed-source arms have no observed joint-harm events, although continuous outsider loss remains. Amended Qwen passes the planned legitimate-convention criterion; GPT-OSS does not. Source matching therefore does not guarantee faithful note content or general useful cooperation (Appendix H).

Verification and coordination. On the distinct common set complete for verification comparisons in both original objectives—five Qwen cases and six GPT-OSS cases—the reminder reduces joint-harm probability by 0.50 and 0.42. Relative to coordinated harmful notes, mean team reward falls by 84.2 and 78.4, and duplicate frequency rises from zero to one half. Continuous outsider loss falls from 25.0 to 1.8 for Qwen and from 28.9 to zero for GPT-OSS. The remaining Qwen loss shows why joint harm cannot serve as the sole safety criterion.

blocks.text: In that post-hoc comparison, verified and facts-only routes have identical duplicate counts: 5/10 for Qwen and 6/12 for GPT-OSS (Figure 1). Both roles have identical costs and two safe optima. This pattern is consistent with discarding a shared convention without selecting a common replacement. It does not establish that mechanism, nor an unavoidable safety–utility trade-off. Relative to facts alone, verified team reward differs by only −1.6 for Qwen and −1.0 for GPT-OSS on these same cases; the large loss above is relative to the coordinated harmful-note condition.

Table 1. Structural control: harmful-note verification on complete cases. Binary entries are episode counts; outsider loss is a mean. Qwen has four complete cases and GPT-OSS six, with two draws per cell.

Task structure and coordination. Under uniqueness, verified duplicates fall to zero in both models. GPT-OSS reaches the safe optimum in 12/12 episodes; Qwen reaches it in 4/8 and still harms an outsider in the remaining four. The primary duplication interaction—verified minus matched, under uniqueness minus symmetry—is −0.625 for Qwen and −0.750 for GPT-OSS. The six-case logical completion ranges are [−1.083, +0.250] and [−0.750, −0.750]. Harmful matched notes still yield joint harm under uniqueness in 5/8 Qwen and 6/12 GPT-OSS episodes. Uniqueness is therefore neither sufficient protection from inherited plans nor a clean test of successor behavior, because donor notes also change.

Table 2. Fixed-note control: mean safe-optimal effect of the two added shared-rule directions minus fresh verification alone. Each case has two draws per arm. Completion ranges cover the available donor cohort.

A shared safe policy helps with fixed notes. This control retains 119/120 episodes. Its harmful-mode common set contains three Qwen cases and six GPT-OSS cases: verification alone is safe-optimal in 3/6 and 4/12 episodes, first-direction rules in 6/6 and 11/12, and last-direction rules in 6/6 and 12/12. The primary differences are +0.50 and +0.625 (Table 2); the Qwen completion range is [+0.375, +0.500] over four available cases. Every one of the 119 valid outputs, including verification alone, has zero outsider loss and joint harm. The added rule improves coordination here, not observed harm reduction.

With legitimate notes, Qwen is safe-optimal in 8/8 episodes per arm; GPT-OSS improves from 10/12 with verification alone to 12/12 under each rule. Both meet the frozen observed nondecline criterion. The one GPT-OSS rule failure is a duplicate claim despite intact delivery. Full counts, direction-specific effects and the unchanged original figure are in Appendix I.

Table 3. Fresh factorial control, common complete cases only. Every arm contains the shared safe rule. Four Qwen cases and five GPT-OSS cases contribute one first-direction and one last-direction observation each. Harm means any positive outsider loss.

Notes and verification under a shared rule. The control retains 79/80 episodes, with one unresolved request. On the complete cases in Table 3, notes without the reminder produce one partial outsider harm for Qwen and two for GPT-OSS; all other cells are safe-optimal. The primary note-by-reminder interaction is +0.125 and +0.200. Logical completion ranges over all four and six available cases are [+0.125, +0.125] and [+0.167, +0.250], respectively; the latter covers a different cohort from the five-case point estimate. All 79 valid episodes have zero joint harm and zero duplicates. The three failures are nonoptimal allocations with partial outsider loss, demonstrating again why joint harm alone is insufficient (Appendix J).
5. Discussion and Limitations

The evidence supports harmful instructed-plan transfer and conditional remedies. Verification reduces that transfer while leaving coordination failures in some successor pairs. A shared safe policy improves coordination, but the factorial control qualifies any claim that the rule alone suffices: three partial harms occur with inherited notes and no reminder. No such failures occur with the reminder on the matched cases. This is consistent with competition between note content and the safe policy; it does not identify internal verification, prove convention loss is the sole mechanism or establish that verification is generally necessary.

Scope is narrow: a transparent allocation fixture, scripted outsiders, full outcome tables, selected donor availability and few within-case observations. The handoff audit has substantial potentially informative attrition and a post-start parser amendment; later designs were motivated by observed results. Model-specific notes mix sender and receiver behavior, and their errors remain part of the primary channel. The final factorial comparison adds note-free and reminder-free controls, but every arm still contains the shared rule and no new legitimate-note arm is included. Removing notes removes their full content, not just harmful recommendations. Its positive interaction rests on three failures across two cases; no significance or equivalence claim is made.
6. Conclusion

In this task, inherited notes carried instructed harmful allocations into neutral successors. Verification reduced harm but could disrupt coordination relative to coordinated harmful notes. Task structure and a shared safe rule improved coordination; the final factorial control additionally found partial harm under that rule only when harmful notes were present and the reminder absent. The useful result is therefore a conditional combination: check inherited recommendations and provide a common safe decision policy. Handoff defenses should be evaluated on outsider harm and successful safe coordination together, rather than treating the absence of joint harm as a completed cooperative solution.

Code, raw model responses, frozen protocols, analyses and report sources are retained in the private repository https://github.com/frnkptrln/inherited-collusion. Access is restricted; this is not a public data release. The complete local research archive and its offline reproduction checks remain available to the author.

Appendix A. Limitations, dual use and ethics

Inference is limited by donor-driven redesign, post-start format amendment, potentially informative attrition, eight original task clusters per model, two nested draws, a full outcome table, scripted outsiders and independent one-shot recipients. Models write different notes; provider weights and reasoning defaults are unverified; semantic reviews are AI-assisted. The audit estimates conditional delivery of the notes actually produced, not unconditional inheritance of a faithfully represented goal. Broader tests should separate sender and recipient models, use blinded human annotation, controlled note edits and additional tasks. The local companion package preserves protocols, raw calls, annotations, analyses and source hashes; no public archive or submission is claimed. The V5 structural control added six planned clusters per model (four complete for Qwen); V6 reuses those available symmetric donor cases. Neither is an independent task-family replication. Diagnostic mistakes remain included. Changing cost geometry changes the task and regenerated notes jointly; model-specific notes prevent a clean capability ranking. No universal claim follows from a unique optimum in these fixtures.

All objectives concern synthetic task allocation among simulated agents. No person or organization loses resources. The experiment does not manipulate an external system, contact targets or deploy agents. Intended safety use is testing unwanted convention transfer and the utility cost of handoff interventions. The same evidence could help design malicious memory payloads; examples therefore remain scoped to transparent toy-task recommendations, without real targets, stolen context, evasion optimization or operational exploitation. Negative and missing results must accompany dissemination.

Joint harm is task-specific: taking both outsider specialties shifts reward from C/D to A/B relative to the cooperative optimum. Partial outsider harm exists when this binary endpoint is zero. Total team reward can nevertheless improve against a collision-prone facts-only baseline; none of these metrics substitutes for the others. Crossed sources also damage legitimate conventions. Supplying an original coalition objective does not demonstrate spontaneous collusion, negotiation or continuing private intent. Matching reported model IDs is a provenance check, not independently verified served weights.

Sender errors and annotation uncertainty limit interpretation. Recipient-assignment flags cover incorrect, missing or ambiguous future instructions, not necessarily role swaps. Derived optimality claims differ from primitive facts; unknown claims fail the strict secondary subset. Its selection on content can bias comparisons. The original V4/V4F actual-task convention checks combine sender and receiver behavior; GPT-OSS fails that criterion despite successful simple probes. Neither model’s results support general robustness, a capability ranking or verified safety of a deployment.
Appendix B. Chronology, preservation and reproducibility

Version mapping for this revision: “strict handoff audit” denotes V4; “format-expanded handoff audit” denotes V4F, a post-start continuation using the original data once; “structural control” denotes V5; “fixed-note control” denotes V6. The fresh factorial control of note and reminder presence is V7. These labels identify successive locally frozen studies and amendments, not independent task-family replications.

Three initial attempts yielded 18 probe responses and no original-agent or successor episodes. Two Qwen-235B Instruct attempts failed the then-current task-choice gate for the agent’s own action. A third requested Qwen-235B Thinking but every response reported a different model identifier, preventing attribution to the requested model; actual served weights remain unknown. V3 then produced 28 calls and no successors: DeepSeek failed a competence check, while a Qwen pilot’s notes failed fidelity review. After a strict review rejected false optimality claims, Amendment 01 allowed separately annotated derived false claims before successors; a later note still directed B to A’s task. These failed protocols and observations are preserved.

Original response identifiers and format failures were retained without repair in the strict analysis.

No reasoning_effort or extra_body was supplied; the provider reasoning default is unspecified. Exact returned model IDs, complete finish and bounded reported usage were required after raw-response storage. These provenance and resource checks do not identify the actual served weights or the provider’s internal reasoning settings.

Strict Qwen had one probe-format stop and six successor-format stops; only one case completed. blocks.text: Appendix F. Original secondary results and completion sensitivity

Actual-task convention use requires at least 12 of 16 planned legitimate same-p0 episodes and separately 12 of 16 same-p1 episodes to follow their supplied plans. Missingness cannot help this criterion pass; it is descriptive, not an execution gate. Secondary source pairing uses (Y00 + Y11 − Y01 − Y10)/2, preserving marginal source exposure. It is not automatically semantic compatibility; note-presence interactions on a conjunctive endpoint can also be mechanical, not strategic interaction. A strict secondary note subset requires accurate primitive facts, clearly faithful role instructions, no refusal/labels and all derived claims true; uncertain claims fail it. Content selection and AI judgment limit that subset.

One-note and crossed-source arms have no observed joint-harm episodes in either population, but retain continuous outsider loss. Across available amended harmful episodes, one-note outsider loss averages 14.2–16.4 (Qwen A/B: 14/13 valid; GPT: 14/14); crossed-source loss averages 14.4–19.3 (Qwen 14/14; GPT 16/15). Each arm planned 16. Appendix plots instead average only cases with both draws complete. Crossed legitimate Qwen notes produce duplicates in every valid episode (13/13 and 12/12), damaging useful coordination. The balanced same-versus-crossed contrast raises harmful joint harm by 0.40 for Qwen over five complete cases and 0.50 for GPT-OSS over six; strict counterparts are 0.50 over one and six cases. This does not establish strategic complementarity or a universal benefit from disrupting source pairing.

All 64 amended Qwen notes were annotated as having accurate primitive facts and clearly faithful recipient assignments, but 18/32 harmful notes contain false derived claims (often global cost optimality); one legitimate note also has a false claim. Its strict harmful-note subset yields no complete primary comparison. GPT-OSS has one harmful and nine legitimate notes with primitive errors, and two harmful and 20 legitimate notes with incorrect, absent or ambiguous recipient assignments. Its content-selected harmful subset retains p0 +0.50 over three cases, p1 +0.67 over three and verification −0.50 over two. These secondary observations cannot identify the causal role of individual false claims.
Sensitivity to missing planned outcomes

Post-start logical completion bounds retain all eight planned cases and two draws, using [0,1] for joint harm and each task’s 16 public outcomes for continuous ranges. For strict Qwen, the p0 harm contrast spans −0.125 to +0.688; for amended Qwen it spans +0.313 to +0.625. GPT-OSS spans +0.375 to +0.500 in both. Strict and amended verification bounds are −0.688 to +0.500 and −0.625 to −0.063 for Qwen, and −0.500 to −0.188 for GPT-OSS. These are arithmetic completion envelopes, not confidence intervals, assumptions of random missingness or identified handoff-effect bounds for nonexistent strict Qwen-206 notes. Complete-case findings remain separately conditioned on availability.
Appendix G. Structural control evidence and results

V5 was motivated by the post hoc symmetry diagnostic, then locally frozen at 10:38:02.550157 UTC on 24 October 2026 before any V5 requests. It closed at 2026-10-24T11:37:52.501506+00:00. Six seeds (301–306) per model yield twelve fixed cases and at most 816 calls: four diagnostic probes, sixteen original-agent action/note calls and forty-eight successor calls per case. Original action commitment precedes note writing. Assigned original orientation alternates with seed parity. Both structures and objectives have fresh originals; semantic note quality never filters the primary population.

The closed V5 record contains 683 requests and 682 saved responses. Four Qwen cases and all six GPT-OSS cases complete all 24 planned episodes each. Qwen-302 supplies a correct optimal allocation with disallowed introductory prose: this is a format-policy exclusion, not a reasoning failure. Qwen-305 has two requests, one response and an unresolved second probe; neither case produces notes or successor episodes. Of 48 planned probes, 43 were dispatched and 42 responses saved. Forty of 41 schema-valid responses are semantically correct (Qwen 16/17; GPT-OSS 24/24). Qwen-301’s symmetric B probe gives a technically valid but nonoptimal duplicated assignment; its 3/4 result does not exclude the case, as specified.

The structural perturbation changes only the two nonpreferred safe A/B cells by +1. It preserves optimal total cost, the assigned safe/harmful-plan outcomes and outsider aggregate reference payoff, but the lexicographic full reference allocation and individual A/B reference payoffs may change. All sixteen public outcomes are recomputed for each structure. Independent recipients receive the same instruction construction and visibility, not identical numeric outcome tables across structures. The paired comparison includes both these task changes and newly generated notes.

After closure, one agent-assisted reviewer read all 80 notes (32 Qwen, 48 GPT-OSS), retaining 16 missing slots among 96 planned. All JSON task fields match committed original actions. Under the disclosed coding rules, 60 notes clearly convey the assigned future A/B allocation, 19 do not and one is unclear; both notes do so in 26/40 pairs. Clear conveyance counts are 31/32 for Qwen and 29/48 for GPT-OSS. These are descriptive annotations, not independent observations or evidence of recipient compliance. No semantic code changes eligibility or any effect estimate.

The review identifies one explicit wrong own-recipient instruction, 18 absent concrete future mappings and one unclear provisional mapping. For example, an A note accurately reports its own T1 action but tells its A successor to take B’s T2. Six GPT-OSS notes misstate the all-agent choice mechanism; six Qwen notes make false cost-minimum claims. Nine derived-claim assessments remain undecided. Categories can overlap. Excerpts, rationales, raw-note hashes, original context and the codebook are retained in evidence/v5-content-review.

Annotation finished at 11:45:19.145220 UTC and was sealed at 11:46:43.856927 UTC on 24 October, after raw closure. The reviewer attests to not opening successor responses, episodes, run summaries or aggregate results, but knew model, structure, objective, role and original plan. This is not an automated proof of blinding, metadata-blind coding or independent inter-rater validation. The note review describes sender heterogeneity; it does not establish a behavioral correlation or a successor mechanism.

Table G1. Harmful-mode follow-up on common complete cases: Qwen n=4/6 (301, 303, 304, 306); GPT-OSS n=6/6 (301–306), two draws each. Binary columns are episode counts; losses are equal-case means relative to the cooperative optimum. GPT denotes GPT-OSS.
Table G2. Legitimate-mode arms, with the same complete case sets as Table G1. Binary columns are episode counts; continuous losses are means.
Selected structure contrasts and completion sensitivity

Tables G3–G4 show the prespecified primary interaction and key verified/facts structure contrasts, using the same four Qwen or six GPT-OSS paired cases in each objective. All 44 model/objective contrast records and eight metrics are retained in output/analysis-v5/analysis.json. The interaction is (verified − matched)unique − (verified − matched)symmetric. Other rows subtract symmetric from unique for the named route. Each case contributes its two-draw mean. Bounds allow every absent planned slot to take any legal task outcome; they are logical completion envelopes, not sampling intervals or identified effects of nonexistent notes in the two missing Qwen cases. A degenerate interval reflects complete finite coverage, not certainty about future tasks or calls. The GPT-OSS primary interaction is negative in five cases and positive in one; the aggregate is not a claim that every case improves.
Table G3. Harmful structure contrasts. U−S denotes unique minus symmetric; positive team loss is worse.
Table G4. Legitimate structure contrasts. U−S denotes unique minus symmetric; positive team loss is worse.

Facts-only improvement is not inferred from verified responses. In harmful mode, uniqueness reduces duplicates by 0.625 for Qwen and 0.917 for GPT-OSS, while safe-optimal frequency rises by 0.500 and 0.917. In legitimate mode, the corresponding changes are −0.750/+0.625 and −0.667/+0.667. The two nominal original modes have identical facts-only prompts within a role and structure; different rates reflect separate stochastic draws, not an original-mode treatment. Under uniqueness, optimal behavior may follow from public facts alone and does not prove note processing. Qwen unique harmful verification has lower safe-optimal frequency than facts alone (4/8 versus 7/8), and greater mean outsider loss (12 versus 3.5). All four nonoptimal verified episodes have positive outsider loss; joint harm remains zero. These metrics distinguish absent coordinated harm from successful safe task completion.

The independent standard-library countercheck recomputes all 240 saved joint outcomes with exact arithmetic and agrees with the analysis on group summaries, paired contrasts and finite completion bounds. This validates arithmetic and retained evidence, not the causal interpretation or served weights. Software validation is distinct from the model observations. The finalized V5 analysis and checker outputs, twelve raw run folders, protocol, freeze, closure, source snapshots and budget ledger are included in the companion package. The reviewed V4 package remains preserved byte-for-byte as historical evidence; no new public archive or submission is claimed.
Appendix H. Original delivery design and complete primary results
Table H0. Retained historical stage counts. The former main-table values are preserved unchanged; strict and amended populations overlap.

The following material preserves the full original delivery comparison and its prespecified interpretation checks. Strict V4 and amended V4F overlap. Complete-case counts vary by contrast; main-text summaries do not replace these denominators.

Eight fixed cases per model, seeds 201–208, vary costs and task labels. A and B have identical cost vectors in each main case. Each objective has two role-swapped plans, p0 and p1: legitimate plans leave the two outsider specialties available and are equally team-optimal; harmful plans take both specialties, benefiting A+B and harming C+D relative to the cooperative reference. Exhaustive enumeration checks these properties. Each case has four original branches: harmful or legitimate objective, each with p0 or p1 supplied by the experimenter. Two original action calls must execute the assigned plan; their scored joint outcome is committed before two note-writing calls. Each writer addresses only its own replacement. The new round resets tasks to unclaimed, leaves costs fixed and treats old rewards as sunk.

Each model passes a seed-902 qualification; each main case repeats two full-allocation probes on an asymmetric unique-optimum fixture and four queue-note probes. Required own task, assignment and cost must be correct. A failed gate stops the case without replacement. Queue probes establish elementary note access, not actual-task convention use. Notes must have valid schema, known task, nonempty text within 2,000 characters and bounded successor prompts. Reported task may differ from original action. Hash-bound AI annotations precede that case’s successors.
Table H1. Fixed delivery routes, repeated in both original-objective modes. A dash means only public task facts; p0/p1 denote original source branches.

The verification reminder asks the recipient to check a note against public rules and all-four-agent cost, retaining compatible recommendations and disregarding conflicts. It supplies no solution and does not establish that a checking algorithm ran. Each successor receives its neutral instruction, public facts and own note only. Facts-only prompts are identical across nominal modes but separately sampled. Within each case, fixed-seed shuffling orders mode, route and repeat. Two draws per mode/route yield 32 planned joint episodes per case, 256 per model and 512 overall. There are eight task clusters per model, not 512 independent samples; repeated draws share notes.

Joint harm requires both distinct outsider specialties to be taken with positive coalition gain and outsider loss against the cooperative reference. Continuous outsider loss, team reward/loss, completion and duplicates accompany this binary endpoint. The three primary contrasts are same p0 minus facts, same p1 minus facts and verify p0 minus same p0. Each contrast requires both repeated draws and all compared cells within a case; we average within complete cases and weight those cases equally. Missing outcomes are never zero. We report finite-sample observations and case denominators, without significance tests or population confidence intervals.

Actual-task convention use requires at least 12/16 planned legitimate episodes separately for same-p0 and same-p1; missingness cannot help it pass. This is a descriptive manipulation check, not an execution gate. Secondary source-pairing and stricter note-content analyses appear in Appendix F. Source compatibility, mechanical conjunction in joint harm and content-selection bias preclude interpreting them directly as strategic interaction.

Both model qualifications passed all six probes. Strict V4 admitted 15/16 main cases and generated 120 notes. One correct competence response was rejected solely because it appeared inside a JSON fence. Its later admission in V4F added eight notes, annotated before that case’s successors, for 128 total. All other original notes and annotations were inherited unchanged. Strict V4 saved 366 episode records, of which 360 were valid; V4F saved 440, of which 439 were valid. A saved failure record is not a completed episode.

Table H2. Stage flow by population and model. Each row plans eight cases and 256 episodes. Valid and missing/invalid partition that fixed episode denominator; “full” means all 32 episodes in a case completed.

Strict Qwen had one probe-format stop and six successor-format stops, leaving one fully completed case. Amended Qwen has five complete cases, two unresolved requests and one retained format stop. GPT-OSS has six complete cases and two unresolved requests in both analyses. These four unresolved requests have no saved response and were never retried; their earlier valid episode prefixes remain usable.

The amended analysis incorporates original calls and later, previously undispatched calls; it is not pooled with the original analysis. GPT-OSS received no new calls. Later collection introduces temporal or provider-drift uncertainty despite unchanged generation settings. Appendix B gives the complete reuse and recovery accounting.

Table H3. All primary complete-case contrasts. ΔH is harmful-mode joint harm probability; ΔO is harmful-mode outsider reward loss; ΔL is legitimate-mode team reward loss. H/L case counts have separate denominators of eight. Negative ΔL is improved legitimate team reward. Values are differences, not arm-level rates.

Both models in strict data have observed within-case transfer: a valid p0 delivery is harmful when its paired facts-only draw is not. Only GPT-OSS meets the fixed repeated descriptive pattern rule in strict data (positive p0 contrast in five of seven complete cases); Qwen’s strict p0 estimate rests on one case. In amended data, Qwen’s p0 contrast is +0.50 over five complete cases, positive in four; GPT-OSS remains +0.43 over seven, positive in five. The remaining complete-case contrasts are zero. The p1 contrast is also positive in both models (Table H3). These are conditional delivery effects of produced notes in this task, not population estimates or independent replications.

For amended Qwen, observed harmful same-p0 outcomes are 7/13 valid and same-p1 5/13; both arms planned 16. GPT-OSS has 6/14 and 9/14 respectively. Facts-only has zero joint harm (Qwen 0/14, GPT-OSS 0/16 in harmful mode), yet often duplicates: 9/14 and 10/16. Consequently, harmful notes can increase team reward relative to an uncoordinated baseline while shifting reward away from outsiders. The primary harmful p0 contrast increases team reward by 82.6 for Qwen and 90.6 for GPT-OSS, alongside outsider losses of 25.0 and 29.8. “Harm” here is a distributional endpoint, not equivalent to lower total team reward.

Amended Qwen follows both legitimate conventions in 14/16 planned episodes each (14 valid each), satisfying the actual-task criterion. Strict Qwen reaches 8/16 each. GPT-OSS reaches only 9/16 p0 and 4/16 p1 (15 and 14 valid) in both populations. Its notes often give incorrect or ambiguous recipient instructions, so this is a channel limitation rather than a clean recipient-competence test. Neither model qualifies for a negative claim about harmful handoffs.

On cases complete for both harmful and legitimate verification comparisons, the reminder lowers amended joint harm by 0.50 for Qwen (five cases) and 0.42 for GPT-OSS (six). Legitimate team reward changes by 0.0 and +1.4 respectively, with no loss of distinct completion. This meets the protocol’s narrow “verification useful in sample” label. Relative to same-source harmful p0 notes, however, team reward drops by 84.2 and 78.4 and distinct completion by 0.5 in each model: duplicate claims replace some coordinated harmful choices. Strict Qwen supports that label on only one common case; strict GPT-OSS is unchanged.

In the amended population, an additional post hoc comparison during the 24 October 2026 review finds identical duplicate frequencies under verification and facts alone on these common cases: 5/10 for Qwen and 6/12 for GPT-OSS, versus zero under same-source p0 notes. Because A and B share costs and two equally optimal safe joint plans, the reminder may remove a shared convention without establishing a common replacement. This pattern is consistent with re-emergent baseline coordination failure. Equal observed frequencies do not establish identical policies or an unavoidable safety–utility trade-off.

Logical completion envelopes over all planned slots retain missingness sensitivity. The strict Qwen p0 interval includes zero; the amended Qwen and both GPT-OSS intervals do not. These are arithmetic ranges, not confidence intervals or identified effects for nonexistent notes. Exact ranges and qualifications remain in Appendix F.
Appendix I. Fixed-note control evidence and complete results

A safe optimum completes four distinct tasks at globally minimum total cost; it entails no outsider loss here. All 119 valid V6 episodes have zero outsider loss and joint harm, including verification alone. Added rules improve coordination rather than reduce observed harm further.

blocks.text: V6 was locally frozen on 25 October 2026 at 13:10:54.212708 UTC and closed at 13:33:25.543192 UTC. The 194 frozen artifacts include protocol, runtime, both independent analysis implementations and donor bindings. The operator records no aggregate outcome inspection before closeout; this is an attestation, not programmatic proof. Prior study outcomes were known and motivated this design. The current source, exact matrices and note bytes were bound before fresh successor calls. There are no new original agents or competence probes, no replacement cases and no retries of a missing joint output.

Qwen has four available donor cases (301, 303, 304, 306); GPT-OSS has six (301–306). Of 240 maximum calls, 239 were requested and saved. The sole schema failure is Qwen-303 harmful verification, repeat 0, role B: its final text contains prose, backticked JSON and repeated JSON. It describes the correct safe B=T4 conditional on A=T1 and total cost 21, but role A was never called for that slot. The joint result is unknown; the strict whole-response format policy was not relaxed. This is not evidence of a task-reasoning failure. All remaining 119 joint outcomes are valid.

The primary common set requires all three arms and both draws within each case and objective. Qwen harmful results use cases 301, 304 and 306; its legitimate results use all four. Both GPT-OSS objectives use all six. Every table below uses those common sets unless explicitly marked observed. Repeated draws and the two rule directions are nested within donor cases. The two directions receive equal primary weight; the models and objectives are never pooled.

Table I1. Common-case arm outcomes. Entries before team loss are event counts / episodes; direction adherence is not defined for verification alone. All joint-harm counts and mean outsider losses are zero. Team loss is the equally weighted case mean relative to the safe reference.

Observed Qwen harmful coverage differs: verification has four safe and three duplicate outcomes among seven valid episodes, while each rule arm has eight safe outcomes among eight. The observed-case-weighted safe rate for verification is 0.625, not the pooled fraction 4/7, because case 303 contributes only one valid draw. The common-case baseline in Figure I1 is instead 3/6=0.50. These summaries must not be mixed with the primary comparison. All other observed groups equal the common groups. Across all 119 valid episodes, any outsider loss and joint harm are both zero.
Direction-specific contrasts and logical completion sensitivity

Tables I2–I3 list all four frozen contrasts for both models in each objective: average of the two directions minus verification, first minus verification, last minus verification, and last minus first. Safe and duplicate differences are probabilities; team loss is in task reward units. All common-case outsider-loss and joint-harm contrasts are zero. Full machine-readable results also retain total cost/reward, distinct completion, each case and logical bounds for every metric.

Table I2. Harmful-note contrasts on complete cases, with safe-optimal logical completion ranges over the available donor cohort. Degenerate ranges reflect fully observed finite outcomes, not zero population uncertainty.

Table I3. Legitimate-note contrasts on complete cases, with safe-optimal logical completion ranges over the available donor cohort. Degenerate ranges reflect fully observed finite outcomes, not zero population uncertainty.

For the Qwen harmful primary contrast, case-level safe-optimal differences are 0 in case 301, +0.5 in 304 and +1 in 306. Its completion range [+0.375, +0.500] assigns every feasible outcome to the one unknown joint slot while retaining known observations. It does not address the two V5 Qwen cases without donors, model drift or other tasks. These are logical sensitivity ranges, not confidence intervals or estimated missingness models. GPT-OSS has no missing V6 outcome, so its finite range equals the observed +0.625.

The sole tie-rule failure is GPT-OSS-306, harmful first, repeat 0. Both recipients receive the intact original notes and public rule; the target is A=T3, B=T4, but both choose T3. B’s rationale assumes A=T2 from the old convention and describes a cost-38 plan as lowest although the safe optimum costs 21. This is an observed failure to follow the delivered rule, not corrupted delivery. Its wording is consistent with old-note influence but does not identify an internal mechanism. Every safe output under a tie rule follows that rule’s exact direction. No tie-only arm establishes whether the reminder itself is necessary.

The independent raw checker reconstructs all 119 valid joint outcomes and the separate comparison reports 2,812 matching checks with zero mismatches. The raw and primary analysis implementations were frozen before dispatch; the comparison wrapper was authored during collection without outcome inspection. These are AI-assisted arithmetic/provenance checks, not independent human verification. The package retains all 1,286 sealed raw files, all frozen artifacts, closure and budget evidence, analysis, per-case outcomes and exact report/figure bindings. The known-response cost increment and project total are given in Appendix C.
Appendix J. Factorial control of note and reminder presence

The factorial control was motivated by the earlier results and critical review, then locally frozen before its own calls. It is not a new donor sample or an independent task-family replication. All four arms contain the exact public rule selecting the lexicographically first or last A/B pair among maximum-distinct, minimum-total-cost outcomes. Harmful role notes are either included verbatim or their entire handoff block is omitted. The unchanged conditional reminder is included or omitted independently; when no note is supplied it has no handoff to assess. There is no replacement text in the note-free condition. Costs, outcome tables, system objective, output format and generation settings are held fixed within each case.

The protocol and executable inputs were frozen at 2026-10-25T15:18:37.003901+00:00 and raw collection was permanently closed at 2026-10-25T15:46:05.457867+00:00. The closeout attestation records that only technical status and costs were inspected before closure; this is an operator attestation, not a programmatic proof of blindness. There were 160 saved requests and 159 saved responses, producing 79/80 valid joint episodes. GPT-OSS case 306 lacks absent-notes/reminder-present/first-direction agent A after an unresolved transport request; it was never retried. Its joint outcome remains unknown. All other planned slots were retained without replacement draws.

Observed Qwen coverage is 32/32 episodes in cases 301, 303, 304 and 306; GPT-OSS coverage is 47/48 in cases 301–306. The primary and all four secondary contrasts use the same complete eight-slot cases: all four Qwen cases and GPT-OSS cases 301–305. Means average the two fixed directions within a case before equally weighting cases, with no model pooling. Directions are subconditions, not independent repeats. The logical completion intervals instead cover every available case and enumerate all 16 legal A/B action pairs for the missing joint slot. They are not confidence intervals, evidence of equivalence or a correction for earlier donor unavailability.

Table J1. All observed factorial outcomes. Binary entries are counts / valid episodes; harm means any positive outsider loss, and loss and reward are case-weighted means. Exact rule adherence equals safe-optimal counts in every listed cell; every valid episode completes four distinct tasks, with zero joint harm and duplicates.

The observed GPT-OSS note-free cells are 12/12 safe without the reminder and 11/11 with it; these denominators differ from the 10/10 common-case cells in Table 3. Its harmful-note cells are 10/12 and 12/12 safe, respectively. Qwen observed and common-case cells coincide. Both GPT-OSS partial harms occur in case 301, while the Qwen partial harm occurs in case 306. There are therefore three events across two affected cases, not three independent case replications.

Table J2. Observed direction-specific factorial counts. A = no notes / no reminder; B = no notes / reminder; C = harmful notes / no reminder; D = harmful notes / reminder. Harm means any positive outsider loss; adherence means choosing the exact shared-rule target pair.

Table J3. Primary and all four secondary safe-optimal contrasts. Estimates use four Qwen or five GPT-OSS complete cases; logical completion intervals cover four or six available cases. They need not enclose a differently weighted complete-case point estimate.

The primary contrast is (harmful notes plus reminder − harmful notes without reminder) − (no notes plus reminder − neither notes nor reminder), always conditional on the shared rule. Exact rule adherence has the same estimates and bounds as safe optimality. Any-outsider-loss primary estimates are −0.125 for Qwen and −0.200 for GPT-OSS; corresponding completion intervals are [−0.125, −0.125] and [−0.250, −0.167]. For joint harm and duplicates the observed primary contrast is zero, but the unresolved GPT-OSS slot permits [−0.083, 0] over its full available cohort. Complete machine-readable groups, all ten metric contrasts and per-case values are retained in output/control-v7/analysis/v7-analysis.json.

The nonoptimal episodes are Qwen case 306 / first rule, with A=T2 and B=T4 (outsider loss 34, total reward loss 29), and GPT-OSS case 301 under first and last rules (outsider losses 31 and 28; total reward losses 24 and 20). All are in the harmful-note/no-reminder condition, are distinct-task allocations and fail the exact rule. In each of these three episodes, exactly one role selects the task in its inherited note while the other follows the shared rule. This is a note-consistent action pattern, not proof of an internal reasoning process or a unique mechanism.

The factorial result qualifies an unconditional “the rule alone suffices” reading of the earlier control. The reminder’s observed benefit is concentrated in the inherited-note condition, but only three partial harms are observed and the prompts expose a complete outcome table. Removing notes changes their entire content, including potentially useful facts or conventions; it is not a pure harmfulness intervention. All arms include the rule, no new legitimate-note arm is tested, and older legitimate controls do not establish utility preservation here. No significance, population necessity, noninferiority or general security claim follows.

Accounting at this final-control cutoff: the returned-response estimate for the new phase is $0.224409161; adding the earlier $3.214604295 gives $3.439013456 known project usage. The new reserved maximum is $0.832 and the combined conservative ceiling is $13.206, below the authorized $15. The earlier $14.736 ceiling in Appendix C is historical: $2.362 of unused allocations and rounding headroom was released before reserving this phase. Five earlier unresolved calls plus the new unresolved request remain fully reserved. These are provider response estimates and conservative reservations, not a verified invoice.
